name: i18n
title: I18n
description: Paraglide JS setup for translated registry components: a Vite plugin that merges per-component message bundles into the Paraglide project, a standalone merge script, and locale-aware date, number, and currency formatters. Ships the hgn-internationalizing-apps agent skill.

files.content:
import { getLocale } from "@/paraglide/runtime"

export const formatDate = (d: Date, opts?: Intl.DateTimeFormatOptions) =>
  new Intl.DateTimeFormat(getLocale(), { dateStyle: "medium", ...opts }).format(d)

export const formatNumber = (n: number, opts?: Intl.NumberFormatOptions) =>
  new Intl.NumberFormat(getLocale(), opts).format(n)

export const formatCurrency = (n: number, currency = "EUR") =>
  new Intl.NumberFormat(getLocale(), { style: "currency", currency }).format(n)

--- name: hgn-internationalizing-apps description: Use when adding or changing user-facing text, adding or switching a language/locale, overriding the wording of a @hoogin component, formatting dates/numbers/currency by locale, installing a translatable @hoogin component, setting up i18n, or debugging strings stuck in the wrong language — in a Vite + TanStack Router app with Paraglide JS and the @hoogin/i18n registry item. user-invocable: true --- # Internationalizing apps Every user-facing string in the app — @hoogin components and your own code — comes from Paraglide messages and renders in the active locale. The locale comes from a cookie and the browser language by default (a locale in the URL is an optional extra), and every translatable @hoogin component ships its own message bundles. ## Contents - [Requires](#requires) - [How it works](#how-it-works) - [Is it set up?](#is-it-set-up) - [Use messages in your own code](#use-messages-in-your-own-code) - [Add a language](#add-a-language) - [Override a component's wording](#override-a-components-wording) - [Switching locale](#switching-locale) - [Install a translatable component](#install-a-translatable-component) - [Conventions](#conventions) - [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting) - [References](#references) --- ## Requires - Bun as package manager and runtime, Vite, TanStack Router, a client SPA. - `@inlang/paraglide-js` — installed by the base item, not by hand. ## How it works A translatable component ships one message bundle per locale (a `registry:file` that installs to `src/messages/registry//.json` — or `messages/registry/...` in a project without `src/`). A Vite plugin merges those with your app's `messages/.json` into `messages/.generated/`, and Paraglide compiles the result into typed functions in `src/paraglide/`. Your app's `messages/.json` is the last path pattern, so it overrides any component string and survives reinstalling the component. Details: `references/architecture.md`. ## Is it set up? It is when `project.inlang/settings.json` exists and `vite.config.ts` lists `registryMessages()` above `paraglideVitePlugin(...)`. If not, follow `references/setup.md` once, then come back here. ## Use messages in your own code Import `m` from `@/paraglide/messages.js` — shadcn doesn't rewrite this path: ```tsx import { m } from "@/paraglide/messages.js"

{m.notesPage_title()}

{m.notesPage_count({ count })} ``` Rules for your own keys: 1. **Every user-facing string is a message**: visible text, `aria-label`, `placeholder`, titles, toasts, and validation messages in zod schemas (see the `hgn-building-forms` skill). 2. **Prefix keys by feature or component** in camelCase: `notesPage_title`, `profileForm_save`. One flat namespace — a key that a @hoogin component already uses overrides that component's wording (see below), so never reuse a component's prefix by accident. 3. **Add every key to every locale's `messages/.json`.** A key missing from one locale doesn't fail the build; those users silently get the base locale's text. 4. **Parameters** go in braces: `"notesPage_count": "{count} notes"` → `m.notesPage_count({ count })`. 5. **Plurals** use Paraglide variants. Copy this shape (it compiles with Paraglide 2.x; `one`/`other` cover English and Dutch, other locales add categories such as `few` or `many` in their own file): ```json "notesPage_count": [ { "declarations": ["input count", "local countPlural = count: plural"], "selectors": ["countPlural"], "match": { "countPlural=one": "{count} note", "countPlural=other": "{count} notes" } } ] ``` Format dates, numbers, and currency with the shipped helpers, so output follows the active locale — not `toLocaleDateString()`, which reads the system locale: ```ts import { formatDate, formatNumber, formatCurrency } from "@/lib/i18n/format" ``` ## Add a language 1. Add the locale to `locales` in `project.inlang/settings.json`. 2. Create `messages/.json` with every key your app's base-locale file has, starting from `{ "$schema": "https://inlang.com/schema/inlang-message-format" }`. 3. Restart `dev`. @hoogin components already translated into that locale switch over; the rest fall back to the base locale until the registry ships a bundle (or you override their keys, below). ## Override a component's wording Add the component's key to your app's `messages/.json`. It's the last path pattern, so it wins and survives reinstalling the component: ```json { "dataTable_next": "Next page" } ``` ## Switching locale Call `setLocale(locale)` from `@/paraglide/runtime.js` (the `@hoogin/locale-toggle` item does). By default it **reloads the page** under every strategy — with the URL strategy it navigates to the localized URL. Two consequences: - `m.*()` calls at module scope (e.g. messages in a zod schema defined outside the component) are safe: they run again after the reload. - `getLocale()` can be read in render without subscribing to anything. Only `setLocale(locale, { reload: false })` breaks this: then module-level messages stay in the old language, so build such schemas inside the component. ## Install a translatable component ```bash bunx --bun shadcn@latest add @hoogin/data-table ``` The CLI copies the component and its message bundles; the first install also pulls `@hoogin/i18n`. With `dev` running, the merge plugin picks up the files; otherwise restart it. ## Conventions - Override wording in `messages/.json`. Never edit installed bundles under `src/messages/registry/` — `shadcn add --overwrite` replaces them; change the wording in the registry instead. - `messages/.generated/` and `src/paraglide/` are build output; the merge plugin and Paraglide own them. ## Troubleshooting | Symptom | Cause | Fix | | --- | --- | --- | | `Property 'x' does not exist` on `m` | messages not merged or compiled | run `bun run i18n`, or restart `dev` | | Can't resolve `@/paraglide/messages` | `outdir` or `@` alias differs | use `outdir: "./src/paraglide"` and map `@` → `src` | | Plugin can't find `project.inlang/settings.json` | Vite started from a workspace root | pass `root` in the plugin options | | `[i18n] Key "x" defined by both "a" and "b"` | two components share a key | rename one with its component prefix | | A string stays in the base language in another locale | key missing from that locale's file, or the component has no bundle for it | add the key to `messages/.json` | | Text stays in the old language after switching | `setLocale(…, { reload: false })` with module-level messages | let `setLocale` reload, or build those messages in the component | | Dev server recompiles in a loop | something else writes `messages/.generated/` | let only the merge plugin write there | ## References - `references/setup.md` — the one-time setup, for an app without Paraglide yet. - `references/architecture.md` — the merge flow, the base item's three files, and why your app's messages win. - `references/localized-urls.md` — optional locale-prefixed and translated URLs, plus the `deLocalizeUrl` absolute-URL gotcha and nav active-state.

# Architecture

Read this to understand what the `@hoogin/i18n` item installs, where messages come
from, and why your app's own bundle always wins. You rarely need it to *use* i18n;
you need it to debug the merge or explain the setup.

## Message flow

```txt
registry item (per component)             your app
src/messages/registry/<c>/<locale>.json   messages/<locale>.json
            │                                       │
            └──────────┬────────────────────────────┘
                       ▼
      merge plugin → messages/.generated/<locale>.json
                       ▼
      Paraglide → src/paraglide/ (typed m.*() functions)
```

The shadcn CLI copies files but can't merge into an existing JSON file, so a
component can't write into your `messages/<locale>.json`. Instead its bundles land
in their own folder, and the merge step combines them. Because your
`messages/<locale>.json` is the **last** `pathPattern`, any project can reword a
component string without touching registry files, and reinstalling a component
never erases those overrides.

The plugin writes a file for **every** locale in `settings.json`, even when no
component translates into it. A component that ships only `en` and `nl` therefore
doesn't break a project that also supports `de` — those keys fall back to the base
locale.

## The three files the base item ships

Installed to `src/i18n/` and `src/lib/i18n/`. They use only `node:` APIs, so they
work whether Vite runs on Bun or Node.

### `src/i18n/vite-plugin-registry-messages.ts`

Resolves paths from Vite's `root`, not `process.cwd()`, so it also works when
started from a Bun workspace root with `bun --filter`.

It exports two functions (read the installed file for the code):

- `mergeRegistryMessages({ root, srcDir, outDir, settings })` — reads every
  `<srcDir>/<component>/<locale>.json`, throws when two components define the
  same key, and writes one `<outDir>/<locale>.json` per locale in
  `settings.json`. A file is only rewritten when its content changes, so
  Paraglide doesn't recompile in a loop. Defaults: `srcDir` is where
  `shadcn add` installs the bundles (`src/messages/registry` when the project
  has a `src/` dir, `messages/registry` otherwise), `outDir` is
  `messages/.generated`, `settings` is `project.inlang/settings.json`.
- `registryMessages(options)` — the Vite plugin. Its `config` hook runs the
  merge with Vite's `root`; in dev it also watches `srcDir` and re-merges on any
  bundle change.

The `config` hook runs before any plugin's `buildStart`, so the merged files exist
before Paraglide compiles them — that is why `registryMessages()` must be listed
**before** `paraglideVitePlugin()`.

### `src/i18n/merge-messages.ts`

Bun runs TypeScript directly, so the merge also runs outside Vite (CI,
type-checking):

```ts
import { mergeRegistryMessages } from "./vite-plugin-registry-messages"
mergeRegistryMessages()
```

### `src/lib/i18n/format.ts`

Locale-aware formatters for the current locale:

```ts
import { getLocale } from "@/paraglide/runtime"

export const formatDate = (d: Date, opts?: Intl.DateTimeFormatOptions) =>
  new Intl.DateTimeFormat(getLocale(), { dateStyle: "medium", ...opts }).format(d)

export const formatNumber = (n: number, opts?: Intl.NumberFormatOptions) =>
  new Intl.NumberFormat(getLocale(), opts).format(n)

export const formatCurrency = (n: number, currency = "EUR") =>
  new Intl.NumberFormat(getLocale(), { style: "currency", currency }).format(n)
```

# Localized URLs

Optional. Only applies when `strategy` includes `"url"` and the router rewrite
from step 5 of `setup.md` is in place — a cookie/browser-language setup has
no locale in the URL and needs none of this.

With the URL strategy, Paraglide only *prefixes* the locale (`/nl/docs`). This reference adds
**translated path segments** (`/nl/documentatie/introductie`) via the router
rewrite, and covers the two traps that come with it.

## Translate the path segments

Give Paraglide a `urlPatterns` list mapping each internal (canonical) path to its
localized form. Add it to `paraglideVitePlugin` in `vite.config.ts`:

```ts
import type { UrlPattern } from "@inlang/paraglide-js"

const urlPatterns: UrlPattern[] = [
  { pattern: "/", localized: [["en", "/"], ["nl", "/nl"]] },
  {
    pattern: "/docs/installation",
    localized: [
      ["en", "/docs/installation"],
      ["nl", "/nl/documentatie/installatie"],
    ],
  },
  {
    pattern: "/docs/components/:component",
    localized: [
      ["en", "/docs/components/:component"],
      ["nl", "/nl/documentatie/componenten/:component"],
    ],
  },
  // ...every route...
  // Last: the fallback wildcard. It must come after the specific patterns.
  {
    pattern: "/:path(.*)?",
    localized: [
      ["en", "/:path(.*)?"],
      ["nl", "/nl/:path(.*)?"],
    ],
  },
]
```

Rules:

- English stays unprefixed (`/docs`); every other locale is prefixed (`/nl/...`).
- URLPattern matches in order, so the wildcard goes **last**.
- Keep truly fixed segments — component and block slugs like `sidebar`,
  `admin-page` — **untranslated**. They are names, and translating them breaks
  every external link. Translate the words around them.
- Keep `emitTsDeclarations: true` on the plugin so `@/paraglide/runtime.js` and
  `@/paraglide/messages.js` have types.

With the router rewrite in place (step 5 of `setup.md`), internal links
stay canonical and TanStack Router resolves routes on the de-localized path while
publishing localized hrefs.

## Trap: `deLocalizeUrl` needs an absolute URL

`deLocalizeUrl(url)` calls `new URL(url)`, so it throws `Invalid URL` on a bare
path. Two more gotchas compound it:

- `useMatches().fullPath` returns a **path** (not a URL), and is `""` before the
  first match resolves.
- A trailing-slash strip with `/\/$/` collapses the root `/` to `""`.

When you compare the current location against a canonical route — breadcrumbs,
active nav state — normalize like this:

```ts
import { deLocalizeUrl } from "@/paraglide/runtime.js"

const path = deLocalizeUrl(new URL(fullPath || "/", location.origin)).pathname
  // Strip a trailing slash, but never turn "/" into "".
  .replace(/(.+)\/$/, "$1")
```

`new URL(fullPath || "/", location.origin)` supplies the origin `deLocalizeUrl`
needs; `/(.+)` requires at least one character before the slash, so `/` survives.
Apply it in both the breadcrumbs builder and the sidebar's nav-main active check —
patching only one leaves the other's highlight broken on `/nl/...` routes.

## `setLocale` under the URL strategy

With `"url"` in the strategy, `setLocale(locale)` navigates to the localized URL
— a full page load, like the reload it does under every other strategy (see the
main skill's "Switching locale"). A locale switcher just calls `setLocale`; see
the shipped `@hoogin/locale-toggle`.

# One-time setup

Read this only when the app has no Paraglide setup yet (no `project.inlang/`
or no `registryMessages()` in `vite.config.ts`). Do it once, before the first
translatable component. The shadcn CLI can't patch
config, so only steps 1–2 are commands; the rest are edits.

1. **Init Paraglide.** `bunx @inlang/paraglide-js@latest init` — creates
   `project.inlang/` and `messages/en.json`. Done when both exist.
2. **Add the base item.** `bunx --bun shadcn@latest add @hoogin/i18n` — installs
   `src/i18n/vite-plugin-registry-messages.ts`, `src/i18n/merge-messages.ts`,
   `src/lib/i18n/format.ts`, `@inlang/paraglide-js`, and the `hgn-internationalizing-apps` skill
   (`.opencode/skills/hgn-internationalizing-apps/`).
3. **Register the merge plugin before Paraglide** in `vite.config.ts`:

   ```ts
   import { paraglideVitePlugin } from "@inlang/paraglide-js"
   import { registryMessages } from "./src/i18n/vite-plugin-registry-messages"

   export default defineConfig({
     plugins: [
       registryMessages(), // first — it writes the files Paraglide compiles
       paraglideVitePlugin({
         project: "./project.inlang",
         outdir: "./src/paraglide",
         emitTsDeclarations: true,
         // Stored choice, then the browser language. Prepend "url" for
         // locale-prefixed URLs (step 5).
         strategy: ["cookie", "preferredLanguage", "baseLocale"],
       }),
     ],
   })
   ```

   Done when `registryMessages()` is listed above `paraglideVitePlugin`. It needs
   no options: it reads the bundles from where `shadcn add` puts them
   (`src/messages/registry`, or `messages/registry` without `src/`).

4. **Point Paraglide at both message sources** in `project.inlang/settings.json`.
   The last pattern wins:

   ```json
   "plugin.inlang.messageFormat": {
     "pathPattern": ["./messages/.generated/{locale}.json", "./messages/{locale}.json"]
   }
   ```

5. **Optional — locale in the URL.** Skip this unless you want `/nl/...` URLs
   (shareable, crawlable per locale). Prepend `"url"` to `strategy` in step 3,
   then rewrite the router's URLs in `router.tsx`:

   ```ts
   import { deLocalizeUrl, localizeUrl } from "@/paraglide/runtime.js"

   export const router = createRouter({
     routeTree,
     rewrite: {
       input: ({ url }) => deLocalizeUrl(url),
       output: ({ url }) => localizeUrl(url),
     },
   })
   ```

   The base locale (`en`) stays unprefixed; every other locale gets `/nl/...`. To
   translate the path segments themselves, see `localized-urls.md`.
   Without this step, switch locales with `setLocale()` from
   `@/paraglide/runtime.js` (the `@hoogin/locale-toggle` item does that).

6. **Ignore generated output** in `.gitignore`: `messages/.generated/` and
   `src/paraglide/`.

7. **Add scripts** to `package.json`:

   ```json
   "i18n": "bun src/i18n/merge-messages.ts && paraglide-js compile --project ./project.inlang --outdir ./src/paraglide --emit-ts-declarations",
   "typecheck": "bun run i18n && tsc --noEmit"
   ```

   `typecheck` merges and compiles first, so a component referencing a missing key
   fails the build.

8. **Tag the document language** in your entry file:

   ```ts
   document.documentElement.lang = getLocale()
   document.documentElement.dir = getTextDirection()
   ```

Done when `bun run dev` starts clean and `import { m } from
"@/paraglide/messages.js"` typechecks.
